summary: Intermittent p99 throughput spike caused by tenant-level gang-scheduling contention in dedicated pool
description:
Issue summary: Customers observed intermittent p99 latency/throughput regressions for AtlasDocs' dedicated capacity pool across multiple small-stream workloads. Impact: Real customer-facing latency spikes causing API timeouts and increased request retries, visible as a 30% throughput drop for the tenant during spikes.

Observed window: 2026-03-04 23:10 - 2026-03-05 02:00 UTC. The pattern is transient (10-60s bursts) and correlates with a high number of concurrent short-lived streaming sessions from the tenant and a collocated neighbor tenant.

Impact details: - API p50 unchanged; p95 increased slightly; p99 increased up to ~2.8x baseline. - Customer reported 5xx retries from app logs and increased client-side backpressure. - No platform-wide outage; isolated to the dedicated reserved pool hosting the customer and a small set of other tenants.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) In a dedicated pool with mixed tenants, start ~500 short streaming connections across two tenants (A = AtlasDocs workload, B = simulated neighbor small-batch streams).
2) Set stream length to 10-30 tokens per request with inter-request interval of 50-200ms to emulate high churn of small streams.
3) Observe p99 latency and GPU queue length via /metrics and per-tenant dashboards; repeat with tenant B removed to compare.
logs_and_metrics: Support timeline: Grafana traces show p99 spikes coincident with abrupt rises in per-GPU kernel-preempt counts and scheduler wait queue growth.
GPU metrics: SM utilization dips from 78% to 54% during spikes while scheduler run-queue and kernel-preempt counters spike; PCIe enqueue latency shows 2-4x increase.
Serving runtime logs: repeated 'preempted_by_owner' and 'stream_coalesce_timeout' events for small-batch inference workers between 23:12-23:40 UTC.
Autoscaler: no scale-up during the first bursts due to cooldown settings; scale response happens after sustained queueing, which is too late for short bursts.
investigation_notes: 2026-03-05 00:15 - Initial triage by Support (Maya): correlated customer error traces with pool-level telemetry; opened INC-20260305-01.
2026-03-05 01:00 - SRE (Santiago) reproduced burst in staging using the small-stream harness; observed same p99 spike behavior when two tenants with many short-lived streams share GPU nodes.

Hypothesis: Gang-scheduling / rapid context-switching for many short-lived streaming connections is causing kernel preemption and inefficient packing on device, leading to transient throughput degradation for affected tenants.
Additional finding: Autoscaler cooldown and slot fragmentation allow bursts to persist; the scheduler's fairness heuristics cause alternating preemptions that reduce SM efficiency during churn.

Staging test: Enabling 'stream_coalesce' reduced p99 amplitude but increased tail of single-request latencies; increasing per-tenant min_batch and raising autoscaler sensitivity improved overall throughput.
Cross-references: Related to historical artifacts in SUP-33489 (fragmentation from small streams) but root cause here is scheduling interaction under short-burst workloads.
comments: Maya Chen (Support) - 2026-03-05: Reached out to AtlasDocs with timeline and asked for peak request samples and client-side logs. Slack thread: #support-dedicated-pools.
AtlasDocs Ops (Priya Kaur) - 2026-03-05: Provided request_id samples and affirmed customer sees retries in their dashboards at the same timestamps. Shared a CloudWatch export and app-side retry logs.

Santiago Ruiz (SRE) - 2026-03-05: Ran controlled repro in staging (harness: https://github.com/redwood-inference/perf-harness/pull/67). Observed kernel preempt spikes and queueing pattern matching prod.

SRE (Santiago) - 2026-03-06: Applied temporary mitigation by moving AtlasDocs to a short-lived isolation reservation (warm-up nodes) and adjusted autoscaler cooldown to 30s in the affected pool. Customer reports immediate improvement.
Maya Chen - 2026-03-07: Notified customer of temporary fix and ETA for permanent scheduler patch. Opened follow-up operational ticket INT-900401 to track scheduler changes and rollout plan.
resolution: Temporary mitigation: migrated AtlasDocs' traffic to an isolation reservation within the dedicated pool and increased autoscaler sensitivity and reduced cooldown to 30s. Enabled stream_coalesce for the pool as an interim measure. Permanent fix: scheduler team to land fairness and preemption-rate limiting patch (PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/scheduler/pull/178) to avoid oscillatory preemptions for many short-lived streams. Post-deploy will include a staged rollout to dedicated pools and an update to the troubleshooting runbook. Follow-ups: INT-900401 (scheduler rollout), add automated test in perf-harness for short-stream gang scenarios, update RLHF-3b quantization packing doc where needed.
postmortem_followup_items: 1) Scheduler: implement preemption-rate limiter and smarter packing heuristics for sub-100-token streams (owner: @scheduler-team, due 2026-03-20).
2) Autoscaler: add burst-mode tuning profile for pools with many short streams and reduce default cooldown in dedicated pools (owner: @autoscale-team, due 2026-03-14).
3) Observability: add a per-tenant 'kernel_preempt' alert and a short-stream pattern detector to trigger early autoscaler scaling (owner: @telemetry, due 2026-03-12).
4) Docs: update dedicated-pool runbook with mitigation steps to isolate noisy tenants and to use reservation warm-up (owner: @support-docs, due 2026-03-11).
